passage:
I'm Francis. When the crash headlines came, I opened the investing page and my finger hovered over the button. Then I remembered Joseph.
Joseph was laid off last winter, in the middle of a fall, and had to sell his units at a bad price just to pay rent. He told me over tea that the loss was not the market's fault. It was that his cushion had been too thin.
So before doing anything, I sat with a notebook. My monthly costs come to 40,000, so six months is 2,40,000. I checked the balance in my savings accounts: 2,55,000, safe and easy to reach. I felt the knot in my chest ease.
Only after that did I look at the investing page again.
— Francis

passage:
Financial-wellness drop-in, counsellor's note, 18 March.
Gurleen came in during the market fall wanting to do something with her investments. Before we talked about the market at all, she said she wanted to check one thing first: whether her emergency money was in place.
She had written her monthly costs on a slip of paper: rent share, groceries, travel, phone, money for her parents. She multiplied by six. Then she checked her savings account and a fixed deposit. Together they covered a little over six months.
She said, "Okay. If I lost my job tomorrow, I wouldn't have to sell anything at a loss. So I don't need to touch my investments today." She looked visibly lighter. She left without making any change, planning to review her investments calmly with a registered adviser in June.
— Noor

passage:
Zainab's diary, Sunday.
The market crashed this week, and my first reaction was to open my investment app and start moving things around. Maria stopped me on the phone: "Before you touch anything, check your emergency money."
So tonight I did. My monthly costs: rent, food, the metro card, my phone, the amount I send Ammi. Six months of that: I wrote the number down. Then I checked the savings account and the recurring deposit. I have almost five months.
So that's the real gap: one month short. If my company cut jobs, I might have to sell investments when they're at their lowest. That's the thing to fix, not the market.
My plan: for the next few months, extra goes into the savings account until it covers six months. I'm not touching the investments. I feel calmer than I did on Wednesday.

qa.q: How many months did Zainab's savings cover?
How does Zainab feel after checking?
qa.a: Zainab feels calmer than on Wednesday, having found the real gap instead of reacting to the crash.
